name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Ezell running with large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
model.rationale: The R+21 district, Ezell's incumbency, and his roughly 34-to-1 fundraising advantage over Hulum leave the Democrat with no visible path. Markets price a Republican win near 96%, consistent with a Safe R forecast.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Mississippi's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Mike Ezell is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. His Democratic challenger, Jeffrey Hulum III, has raised under $30,000, while Ezell has raised nearly $1 million. An independent, Carl Boyanton, is also on the ballot but is not seen as a significant factor.

No public polling or expert race ratings are available, but prediction markets give Ezell roughly a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and district lean all point the same direction, making this a Safe Republican seat with little realistic prospect of an upset.
